title: Jellyfin no longer binds to all local addresses after updating from 10.8.13 to 10.9.1
body: After updating Jellyfin from 10.8.13 to 10.9.1 on Ubuntu Jammy bare metal, it no longer binds to my local 192.168.1.109 address. It still binds to localhost, my VPN address, and unexpectedly 1.2.3.4. Networking is configured to bind to all addresses, and removing networking.xml so it would be recreated did not change this. Explicitly listing every relevant address under Networking > Bind to local network address is a workaround, but this was not required in 10.8.13. The startup log lists the normal private LAN ranges but reports bind addresses of 127.0.0.1, 1.2.3.4, and 10.1.1.2.

symptoms_visible: After the update, I cannot reach Jellyfin through 192.168.1.109 even though it is configured to bind to all addresses.
The startup log lists bind addresses 127.0.0.1, 1.2.3.4, and 10.1.1.2 instead of including 192.168.1.109.
Removing networking.xml does not change the behavior; explicitly listing the relevant addresses is a workaround.
N0.label: N0 local interface omitted at startup

symptoms_visible: Jellyfin remains inaccessible at 192.168.1.109, while the address appears on my physical enp5s0 interface when I inspect the system after startup.
N1.label: N1 interface inventory collected

symptoms_visible: Removing the Cockpit-created fake0 interface does not restore access through 192.168.1.109.
N2.label: N2 startup context and dummy interface checked

symptoms_visible: After setting IgnoreVirtualInterfaces to false, Jellyfin is still inaccessible through 192.168.1.109.
N2_x.label: N2_x virtual-interface setting aftermath

symptoms_visible: At the moment Jellyfin starts during boot, enp5s0 has no 192.168.1.109 IPv4 address yet.
The local IPv4 address is assigned later, but Jellyfin remains inaccessible through it.
N3.label: N3 boot timing established

symptoms_visible: Immediately after startup, the debug log reports a network address change and then discovers 192.168.1.109.
Even after that refresh lists 192.168.1.109 as a bind address, I still cannot access the web interface there.
Restarting Jellyfin after the interfaces are up makes the web interface reachable.
N4.label: N4 late discovery does not update listener

symptoms_visible: After delaying Jellyfin startup until my WireGuard service is up, Jellyfin starts after the main address has been assigned and I can access it through 192.168.1.109.
N5.label: N5 startup-delay workaround active

symptoms_visible: My startup-delay workaround keeps the web interface reachable at 192.168.1.109.
I have not reported testing the normal boot sequence on a build containing the wildcard-listener change.
N_terminal.label: terminal diagnosis accepted but permanent fix not reporter-verified

question_patterns: Can you show the output of ip addr show?
Which interfaces and addresses exist on the host after boot?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My ip addr output shows 192.168.1.109/24 on enp5s0, 1.2.3.4/24 on fake0, 10.170.37.84 on airvpn, 10.1.1.2/24 on wg0, 172.17.0.1/16 on docker0, and 127.0.0.1 on loopback.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The host never receives 192.168.1.109 on any interface, even long after boot.
The same interfaces are present, but the LAN address is assigned to a differently named physical Ethernet interface.

edges.comment: Reporter c6: raw ip addr output from reporter's Ubuntu bare-metal host. Docker deployments discussed by other participants are not folded into this causal chain.

question_patterns: What creates the fake0 interface, and does removing it change the problem?
Can you temporarily remove the unusual dummy interface and check whether the local address becomes reachable?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: fake0 is a dummy interface created by Cockpit. I removed the interface and Cockpit, but that did not help.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Removing fake0 immediately makes Jellyfin listen on 192.168.1.109 after a normal boot.

question_patterns: Can you reboot and run systemd-analyze plot, then share the resulting startup timeline?
Please capture the boot service timeline so we can compare Jellyfin startup with network initialization.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I rebooted, ran systemd-analyze plot > startup.svg, and posted the resulting startup timeline.

edges.comment: Reporter c20: reporter explains fake0 and supplies the requested startup plot. The remote GitHub image is not listed because no local attachment path was provided.

solution.intent: Include virtual interfaces in Jellyfin's interface selection by setting IgnoreVirtualInterfaces to false.
solution.concrete_example: Change <IgnoreVirtualInterfaces>true</IgnoreVirtualInterfaces> to false in network.xml and restart Jellyfin.

edges.comment: Other user c18 suggested changing IgnoreVirtualInterfaces; reporter c21 tried it and stated it did not help because the affected LAN adapter is not virtual.

question_patterns: At the exact time Jellyfin starts during boot, what addresses are present on the physical LAN interface?
Can you compare the service startup timestamps with the point at which the LAN IPv4 address is assigned?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: At 08:40:49 Jellyfin starts while enp5s0 is up but only has a tentative link-local IPv6 address. It does not have 192.168.1.109 yet. The IPv4 address is assigned after Jellyfin has already selected its bind addresses.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The boot log shows 192.168.1.109 assigned to enp5s0 well before Jellyfin starts, but Jellyfin still omits it.
The LAN IPv4 address arrives a few seconds later than in my original log, but still after Jellyfin starts.

edges.comment: Reporter c22: reporter instrumented startup and pasted timestamped raw output showing that Jellyfin starts before DHCP assigns the physical LAN IPv4 address. The causal conclusion is consumed later rather than inserted into the measurement answer.

question_patterns: Can you enable debug logging and check whether network address or availability change messages appear?
After the LAN address arrives, what does Jellyfin's debug log say about refreshed interfaces and bind addresses?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Immediately after startup I get 'Network address change detected', followed by 'Refreshing interfaces'. It discovers 127.0.0.1, 192.168.1.109, 10.1.1.2, and 172.17.0.1, and then logs bind addresses 192.168.1.109 and 10.1.1.2.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No network-change message appears, and the refreshed interface list never contains 192.168.1.109.
The same refresh and address discovery occur, but a second later than in the original log.

question_patterns: Once the debug log discovers the new address, can you access the web interface through it without restarting Jellyfin?
Does the newly logged bind address actually begin accepting web connections?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. Even though the refreshed log includes 192.168.1.109, I still cannot access Jellyfin there.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, the web interface becomes reachable on 192.168.1.109 as soon as the refresh discovers it.

question_patterns: What happens if you restart Jellyfin after all interfaces have their addresses?
Does a service restart after boot make the LAN web interface reachable?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Restarting Jellyfin after the interfaces are up fixes it; the web interface then works on 192.168.1.109.

edges.comment: Reporter c35-c36, with restart behavior also established in the discussion: reporter supplies raw debug lines and confirms that discovery updates Jellyfin's network inventory but not web accessibility.

solution.intent: Work around the boot race by ordering Jellyfin after a service that only starts once the required network connectivity is available.
solution.concrete_example: On this host, set Jellyfin's systemd unit to start After=<email-scrubbed> so the LAN address has been assigned before Jellyfin starts.

edges.comment: Reporter c24: reporter kept a systemd ordering workaround that delays Jellyfin until <email-scrubbed> is up, restoring access on the reporter's own bare-metal host. This is operational mitigation, not the accepted application-level fix.

solution.intent: Fix the regression by using wildcard listeners when bind-all is configured, so the web server can accept connections on addresses that appear after process startup instead of relying on a startup-time enumeration of interfaces.
solution.concrete_example: When the administrator selects bind to all addresses, configure the web listener on 0.0.0.0 and/or :: rather than only the concrete addresses visible during startup. Then ask the reporter to remove the startup-delay workaround, boot normally, and verify that 192.168.1.109 is reachable after DHCP assigns it.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter showed that Jellyfin's network manager discovers 192.168.1.109 after startup but the web interface remains unreachable. Maintainers then established that Kestrel cannot reload its listener configuration on the fly and that the durable direction is wildcard binding when bind-all is selected. That listener-level conclusion is engineer inference, not part of the reporter's raw debug output.

edges.comment: Maintainer c37-c39 gives the final accepted diagnosis: Kestrel does not relisten when a late address is discovered, so wildcard binding is needed for unpredictable interface timing. A linked PR was mentioned, but the supplied thread does not include an affected-user retest of a build containing it; the terminal therefore remains unverified.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: Jellyfin starts before DHCP assigns the physical LAN IPv4 address, and its web listener is configured from the concrete addresses available at startup; later network refreshes discover the address but do not make Kestrel relisten.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected boot and debug evidence: 192.168.1.109 is absent when Jellyfin starts, appears in a later interface refresh, remains unreachable, and works after restarting Jellyfin once the interfaces are ready.
The durable fix must preserve bind-all behavior by using wildcard listeners rather than depending only on startup-time interface enumeration.
May offer delayed systemd startup or a post-boot service restart as a temporary workaround, but must not present it as the application-level fix.
Must not recommend deleting networking.xml or setting IgnoreVirtualInterfaces to false as the resolution; both directions were tried without resolving this reporter's problem.
Must ask the reporter to test a build containing the wildcard-listener fix under a normal boot without the startup-delay workaround before declaring the permanent issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux administrator running Jellyfin on Ubuntu bare metal; comfortable editing systemd units and XML configuration, collecting ip addr and boot timing output, and enabling debug logging.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, cooperative, and evidence-driven; quotes requested output, tests proposed changes, distinguishes workarounds from proper fixes, and challenges conclusions constructively.
